subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Twelve in the Clock
description: A micro-lesson that makes Twelve in the Clock usable.

hook.text: We divide the day into two sets of twelve. Not ten. Not eight. Twelve—a choice made in Babylon 4,000 years ago.

buildup.text: Babylonians used base-60 math. Sixty divides by twelve. That's why we have 60 minutes and 12 hour marks.

discovery.text: The French Revolution tried a decimal clock: 10 hours, 100 minutes. It lasted two years. Twelve won.

twist.text: We could measure time in any base. But twelve is so deeply encoded in culture that changing it feels wrong.

climax.text: Every time you check the clock, you're reading a Babylonian system filtered through sacred number symbolism.

punchline.text: Babylon built your watch. You just didn't know.

quiz.question: Why did the French revolutionary decimal clock fail?
options: Twelve-based time was too culturally entrenched
